titulo: Relative clauses 2: the relative pronoun in the accusative and «was»: The relative pronoun in the accusative

aula.titulo: Relative clauses 2: the relative pronoun in the accusative and «was»
aula.objetivo: Form relative clauses where the relative pronoun is the direct object (den, die, das, die), use «was» after alles, nichts, etwas and superlatives, and combine several relative clauses.

sessao.titulo: The relative pronoun in the accusative

blocos.titulo: The relative pronoun in the accusative, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: when the relative pronoun is the DIRECT OBJECT of the relative clause, it goes into the ACCUSATIVE: «Der Mann, den ich gestern getroffen habe, ist mein Chef» (the man (whom) I met yesterday is my boss). STEP 2: the forms are those of the definite article in the accusative: «den» (m), «die» (f), «das» (n), «die» (plural). STEP 3: only the MASCULINE changes compared to the nominative (der → den); feminine, neuter and plural stay the same: «die Frau, die ich kenne», «das Buch, das ich lese», «die Filme, die ich mag». STEP 4: the SUBJECT of the relative clause comes AFTER the relative pronoun («den ich», «die ich»): if a noun or pronoun follows the relative pronoun, that's the subject, and the relative pronoun is the object. STEP 5: the conjugated verb stays at the END. And remember: English can drop "that/whom" here ("the man I met"); German never drops it.
blocos.comparacao: English uses the same "that" for subject and object ("the man that lives here", "the man that I met") — or drops it. German shows the difference with the CASE of the relative pronoun: der (subject) × den (direct object, masculine) — just like the old English pair who × whom.

tabela.exemplo: Der Mann, den ich gestern getroffen habe, ist mein Chef.
Die Frau, die ich kenne, arbeitet hier.
Das Buch, das ich lese, ist spannend.
Die Filme, die ich mag, sind alt.

erros.errado: Der Mann, der ich gestern getroffen habe, ist mein Chef.
erros.certo: Der Mann, den ich gestern getroffen habe, ist mein Chef.

erros.errado: Das Buch, den ich lese, ist spannend.
erros.certo: Das Buch, das ich lese, ist spannend.

erros.errado: Der Film, den ich habe gesehen, war gut.
erros.certo: Der Film, den ich gesehen habe, war gut.

blocos.enunciado: Describe 6 things or people out loud with accusative relative clauses: «Das Buch, das ich lese … Der Film, den ich … habe»
Write 6 sentences with nominative relative clauses.
